cards.explanation: The answer is a nearer kinsman-redeemer. The text says the kinsman-redeemer of whom Boaz had spoken came along (Ruth 4:1). Back on the threshing floor, Boaz told Ruth there was a kinsman-redeemer nearer than he was (Ruth 3:12). Boaz sat down and the very man he needed walked right up to him, friends.

The answer is elders. Boaz took ten of the elders of the city and said, "Sit here," and they did so (Ruth 4:2). Ten leaders, all sitting down, and the whole thing is out in the open. That's one witness table you do NOT want to argue with, friends.

The answer is False. Boaz tells the man, "…there is no one but you to redeem it, and I am next after you." (Ruth 4:4). The other man is first, and Boaz stands right behind him. Boaz is not pushing his way to the front of this line, friends.
The answer is "I will redeem it." The man answers Boaz, "I will redeem it…" (Ruth 4:4). That is his answer about the land. And Boaz has one more thing to say to him next, bakers (Ruth 4:5).

The answer is that he must acquire the widow of the deceased. Boaz says that on the day the man buys the land from Naomi and Ruth the Moabitess, he must also acquire the widow of the deceased, in order to raise up the name of the deceased on his inheritance (Ruth 4:5). So the land comes with Ruth, and that changes the whole deal. Boaz laid it out plainly, friends, no fine print.

The answer is False. The man says, "I cannot redeem it myself, or I would jeopardize my own inheritance." (Ruth 4:6). Earlier he had said, "I will redeem it…" (Ruth 4:4), and then Boaz added Ruth to the deal (Ruth 4:5). Once Ruth is part of the deal, his answer changes, friends.

The answer is that it would jeopardize his own inheritance. He says, "I cannot redeem it myself, or I would jeopardize my own inheritance." (Ruth 4:6). That's the reason he gives, friends, and the text gives no other. So he steps aside and asks Boaz to take his right of redemption.

The answer is "Buy it for yourself." He removes his sandal and tells Boaz, "Buy it for yourself." (Ruth 4:8). That hands the right of redemption over to Boaz. And that sandal is the confirmation, friends, since in former times in Israel a man would remove his sandal and give it to the other party to make a matter legally binding (Ruth 4:7).

The answer is True. Boaz says to the elders and all the people, "You are witnesses today that I am buying from Naomi all that belonged to Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon." (Ruth 4:9). Elimelech was Naomi's husband, and Chilion and Mahlon were their sons (Ruth 1:2). Boaz is calling in the whole crowd as witnesses, friends, and that is a big, public yes.

The answer is name. Boaz says he has acquired Ruth "…so that his name will not disappear from among his brothers or from the gate of his home." (Ruth 4:10). The name in question is Mahlon's, Ruth's late husband. Boaz is making sure that name stays standing, bakers.

The answer is Rachel and Leah. The people at the gate say, "May the LORD make the woman entering your home like Rachel and Leah, who together built up the house of Israel." (Ruth 4:11). They are sisters, and both were wives of Jacob (Genesis 29:23, 28). That's a big name to say over Ruth, friends, and the whole gate said it.

The answer is offspring. The crowd wishes that Boaz's house may become like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, "…because of the offspring the LORD will give you by this young woman." (Ruth 4:12). Offspring is the word they use, friends.

The answer is True. The text says that when Boaz had relations with Ruth, "…the LORD enabled her to conceive, and she gave birth to a son." (Ruth 4:13). The text credits the LORD for it, friends. A son is born.

The answer is a kinsman-redeemer. The women say, "Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you this day without a kinsman-redeemer." (Ruth 4:14). They are speaking to Naomi, and they start by blessing the LORD. After her hard words earlier (Ruth 1:20-21), that is a big turn for her, friends.

The answer is that he will sustain her in her old age. The women say, "He will renew your life and sustain you in your old age." (Ruth 4:15). They're telling Naomi this about the baby. Renew her life and sustain her, friends. That's a lot to put on one little guy.
The answer is True. The women say Naomi's daughter-in-law "…loves you and is better to you than seven sons…" (Ruth 4:15). That is a big compliment, friends. Seven sons is the number they name.

The answer is True. The text says, "…Naomi took the child, placed him on her lap, and became a nurse to him." (Ruth 4:16). The baby is right there in her lap. After all that, friends, I think she held on tight.

The answer is False. The neighbor women are the ones who say, "A son has been born to Naomi…" and they named him Obed (Ruth 4:17). So the naming comes from the neighbors, friends. The text doesn't say Boaz or Ruth did it.

The answer is David. Ruth 4:17 says Obed "…became the father of Jesse, the father of David." David later became king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3). The book ends by tracing the line from Perez down to David, friends (Ruth 4:18-22).
